The wonderful thing about the draw-flip cycle is that *every* stimulus type follows it. Images work exactly like text: swap `TextStim` for `ImageStim`:

```python
img = visual.ImageStim(win, image='stimuli/stimulus1_L.jpg')
img.draw()
win.flip()
```

::: {.callout-warning title="Paths are relative to your script"}
`'stimuli/stimulus1_L.jpg'` means: *a folder called `stimuli`, next to this script, containing that file*. If your script lives somewhere else, this line fails. Keep your scripts in the workshop folder, next to `stimuli/`. (Roughly half of all "my code doesn't work" moments today will be path problems).
:::

## Two ways to wait

After a flip, we decide how long the stimulus stays. There are two fundamentally different answers, and choosing between them is an *experimental design decision*:

```python
core.wait(2)        # the COMPUTER decides: exactly 2 seconds
event.waitKeys()    # the PARTICIPANT decides: waits for a key press
```

::: {.callout-note .predict icon="false" title="🔮 Predict first — which wait for which screen?"}
For each screen, decide: `core.wait()` or `event.waitKeys()`?

(a) an instructions screen · (b) a feedback screen after a response · (c) a brief fixation cross between trials · (d) a word in a self-paced reading experiment

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Check your prediction"}
(a) `waitKeys()`: people read at different speeds. (b) `wait()`: fixed, comparable duration for everyone. (c) `wait()`: fixed and short. (d) `waitKeys()`: the whole point of *self-paced* reading is that the participant controls the pace; the time they take **is** the measurement. More on that in Session 3.
:::
:::

## Try it

Modify your Chapter 3 script: after the *Hello, world!* screen, show **one CogWheel image** (pick any file from `stimuli/`), participant-paced. Run it.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show the code"}
```python
from psychopy import visual, event, core

win = visual.Window(size=(1280, 720), color='black')

text = visual.TextStim(win, text='Hello, world!',
                       color='white', height=0.1)
text.draw()
win.flip()
event.waitKeys()

img = visual.ImageStim(win, image='stimuli/stimulus1_L.jpg')
img.draw()
win.flip()
event.waitKeys()

win.close()
core.quit()
```

Note the pattern repeating: prepare, draw, flip, wait — once per screen.
:::
